rv.q: 'Other Desert Cities' is the best thing I've seen at the Old Vic in yonks.
Lindsay Posner's pitch-perfect production in a reconfigured theatre-in-the-round is beautifully performed, especially by Cusack, who will surely feature on the year's awards lists.

In drama, a Christmas tree in one comer and a well-stocked drinks trolley in anothergenerally spell trouble- and OtherDesertCities (given its UK premiere in the beautifully reconfigured Old Vic in-the-round) does not disappoint.
This show will not stop the world, but it is not without interest.

In spite of some snappy dialogue and a set of sterling performances from Cusack's terrifyingly intractable mother to Clare Higgins as her former alcoholic sister Silda, the play strives for a significance it doesn't fully merit.

Sinead Cusack and a bewigged Peter Egan happen to be very good at essaying the kind of poised, perma-tanned, dead-eyed couple that anyone who has ever visited a golf club in California will know only too well.
